source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αφροδίσιος, Μίσδας, Μακρόβιος, Ουαλεριανός, Λεόντιος, Αντωνίνος οι Μάρτυρες και οι συν αυτοίς εν Σκυθουπόλει (Συρίας) μαρτυρησάντων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and enumerates the company by name, so this is one of six folders. **He is none of the corpus's seven other Leontii** — of Tripoli, of the Brazen Gate, of Rădăuți, the disciple of Cronides, one of the Forty of Sebaste, the martyr of 16 October, and Karyagin of Kazan — and the place is what tells him from them. **His couplet is the one that names a seventh man**: it is headed «Eις τον Λεόντιον, Aντωνίνον και Mέλη» and reads «O Λεόντιος και συναθληταί δύω, / Λέοντες οίον έδραμον προς το ξίφος» — Leontius and two fellow-contenders ran to the sword like lions. Two fellow-contenders, and the heading names Antoninus and a Μέλης whom the listing and the six head lines do not know. **No folder was made for that name**, because nothing on the page establishes it as a person, and the discrepancy is recorded on every folder of this company. The couplet says sword and the story says stones and clubs; both are printed. No year, no emperor, no hymn, no relic.
